title: Structural-Entropy-Based Sample Selection for Efficient and Effective Learning

contributions.purpose: Incorporate global graph structure (connectivity patterns) into sample selection, which existing local-information methods overlook, and do so tractably.
contributions.mechanism: A node-level structural entropy metric: graph-level structural entropy is losslessly decomposed to individual nodes via the Shapley value (marginal contribution of a node to structural entropy); the Shapley value is reformulated to allow linear-time computation w.r.t. edge count instead of exponential subgraph enumeration.
contributions.evaluation: Theoretical result plus empirical validation (Appendix C): maximizing node-level structural entropy Se(u) lower-bounds/improves sample coverage; on GMM synthetic data matching CIFAR10 stats, the bound ratio lies in 1.00-1.45 for 90% of samples, <1.97 for 99%.
contributions.source_quote: We propose a node-level structural entropy metric that quantifies the importance of nodes in preserving the global structure, and it can be calculated in linear time.

contributions.purpose: Select informative and representative samples under data budgets by combining global and local signals.
contributions.mechanism: SES (Structural-Entropy-based Sample Selection): build a kNN sample graph, score sample importance as the product of node-level structural entropy (global) and training difficulty (local), then apply importance-biased blue noise sampling to iteratively pick diverse, representative samples.
contributions.evaluation: Ablation (Table 4) shows structural entropy (SE) and blue noise sampling (BNS) each improve over TD+highest-score baseline and are complementary; BNS matches D2Pruning message-passing without its grid search.
contributions.source_quote: We develop a structural-entropy-based sample selection method that integrates both global and local metrics to selectinformative and representative samples.

contributions.purpose: Demonstrate that integrating global and local information yields better selection than state-of-the-art methods across diverse learning settings and tasks.
contributions.mechanism: Comprehensive experiments across supervised, active, and continual learning covering image classification, text classification, object detection, and VQA, compared against Random, Moderate, CCS, D2Pruning, GraphCut, and task-specific baselines (Entropy, Forgetting, EL2N, AUM, Variance, k-means, k-DPP, AL-MDN, etc.).
contributions.evaluation: Consistently outperforms baselines across all three scenarios and tasks; e.g. +5.52% accuracy selecting 2% of ImageNet-1K; consistent gains in active and continual learning (Tables 17-21).
contributions.source_quote: We conduct experiments in supervised learning, active learning, and continual learning that demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

self_declared_provenance.quote: The intra-community connection, vol(a), ... structural entropy of G is the aggregation of the entropy values from all its non-root nodes: (based on Li & Pan, 2016)

there are two methods for constructing the encoding tree: the one proposed by Li & Pan (2016) and the one proposed by Zhu et al. (2023) ... In this paper, we employ the more recent method proposed by Zhu et al. (2023).
Without BNS, we either select samples with the highest scores (HS) or use the message passing (MP) method from D2 pruning (Maharana et al., 2024).

notes: Method paper with mostly positive results. Authors are unusually candid about where gains are limited (near-null/comparable regimes, a project signal): they explicitly list settings with little improvement over baselines - high sampling rate on simple datasets (70% CIFAR10, all methods near full-set), very low sampling rate on hard datasets (1% ImageNet-1K), and fine-tuning-from-pretrained scenarios where pretrained knowledge anchors performance. kNN k too large can cause performance decline (underfitting). Encoding-tree construction choice has negligible effect (Pearson >0.99). Best-case improvement +5.52% (2% ImageNet-1K). Limitations noted: manual grid-search hyperparameters, limited multimodal support.
